title: Agentic AI Engineering
description: Build useful AI agents through practical lessons on context, memory, retrieval, tools, workflow design and multi-agent architecture.
tagline: Design and build useful AI agents.

modules.title: Agent Foundations
modules.description: Choose an appropriate agent architecture and build a bounded tool-using loop.

articles.title: Chatbots, Workflows and Agents: Choosing the Right Approach
articles.summary: Choose between a conversational interface, a predictable workflow and a tool-using agent by examining uncertainty, permissions and success criteria.
articles.seoTitle: Chatbots, Workflows and Agents: How to Choose
articles.seoDescription: Choose the right AI architecture for a task. Compare chatbots, fixed workflows and agents with a practical support example and design exercise.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

articles.coverConcept: Three distinct paths: a question-answer pair, a fixed three-stage workflow, and a bounded branching tool loop.
articles.coverAlt: Three architecture choices: conversation, fixed workflow and bounded agent loop.

articles.title: Anatomy of an AI Agent: Model, Tools, State and Control
articles.summary: Understand how models, tool contracts, state and application control work together in an agent, using an evidence-based delivery investigation.
articles.seoTitle: Anatomy of an AI Agent: Model, Tools and State
articles.seoDescription: Learn the components of an AI agent: model, tools, state, evidence and execution control. Follow a worked example and design a state record.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

articles.coverConcept: A five-component architecture linking user goal, model decision, validated tool, state store and final response, with a control boundary.
articles.coverAlt: Agent architecture showing model, tools, state and execution control.

diagram.caption: The controller validates model proposals and records tool observations as evidence.

articles.title: Build Your First Tool-Using Agent
articles.summary: Implement a provider-neutral, read-only agent loop with validated tool calls, explicit limits and grounded final answers.
articles.seoTitle: Build Your First Tool-Using AI Agent
articles.seoDescription: Build a bounded, read-only agent with tool validation, execution limits and source-based answers. Includes provider-neutral pseudocode and exercises.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

articles.coverConcept: A numbered execution loop from user request to proposal, schema validation, authorized lookup, observation and grounded final answer.
articles.coverAlt: Bounded tool loop with validation and a final answer checkpoint.

diagram.caption: A bounded tool loop continues only while validated actions add useful evidence.

modules.title: Context Engineering
modules.description: Build deliberate context packages, clear instructions and task-specific evidence selection.

articles.title: From Prompt Engineering to Context Engineering
articles.summary: Design the complete information package an agent needs at each step, including instructions, evidence, tool contracts and current task state.
articles.seoTitle: From Prompt Engineering to Context Engineering
articles.seoDescription: Learn to assemble useful agent context from instructions, task state, tools and evidence. Includes an evidence-packet example and a practical audit.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

articles.coverConcept: Four input lanes for instructions, current task, selected evidence and tool contracts converge into a bounded model context window.
articles.coverAlt: Instructions, task state, evidence and tools feeding a bounded context window.

diagram.caption: Context construction combines distinct information types for the next model decision.

articles.title: Designing Instructions, Examples and Structured Outputs
articles.summary: Write testable agent instructions, choose examples that teach boundaries and validate structured outputs independently of language-model fluency.
articles.seoTitle: Agent Instructions, Examples and Structured Outputs
articles.seoDescription: Write clear agent instructions and useful examples. Design structured outputs with schema validation, semantic checks and explicit uncertainty.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

articles.coverConcept: An instruction contract and contrasting examples enter a model, followed by schema validation and a separate semantic evidence check.
articles.coverAlt: Instruction and example inputs followed by schema and evidence validation.

diagram.caption: Structured responses require both shape validation and checks against actual evidence.

articles.title: Selecting the Right Context for Each Task
articles.summary: Build a task-aware selection policy that balances relevance, freshness, permissions and evidence coverage within a finite context budget.
articles.seoTitle: Selecting the Right Context for an AI Agent
articles.seoDescription: Design a context selection policy using task relevance, access, freshness and coverage. Work through competing records and test missing evidence.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

articles.coverConcept: Candidate records pass access and freshness gates, branch into supporting and conflicting evidence, then form a compact task packet.
articles.coverAlt: Evidence selection with access, freshness and contradiction checks.

diagram.caption: Select permitted, applicable evidence that covers the question and preserves contradictions.

modules.title: Memory & Knowledge
modules.description: Design evidence-aware memory and retrieval over permitted business information.

articles.title: Session State, Working Memory and Long-Term Memory
articles.summary: Separate session state, compact working memory and persistent user memory with provenance, expiry and appropriate access controls.
articles.seoTitle: Session State and Long-Term Memory for AI Agents
articles.seoDescription: Design agent memory with clear scopes, evidence, retention and correction. Compare task state, working summaries and persistent preferences.
articles.coverConcept: Three memory stores for session events, working summary and verified persistent preferences with different retention clocks.
articles.coverAlt: Session, working and persistent memory stores with distinct lifecycles.

diagram.caption: Working memory draws from current events and separately governed persistent facts.

articles.title: Building RAG with Your Business Documents
articles.summary: Build a retrieval-augmented answer pipeline that preserves document identity, access scope, effective dates and supporting passages.
articles.seoTitle: Build RAG with Business Documents
articles.seoDescription: Build a RAG pipeline for business documents with access filters, useful chunks, source metadata and evidence-based answers. Includes a worked example.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

articles.coverConcept: Business documents become versioned chunks, pass permission-aware retrieval, and produce a cited answer with source passages.
articles.coverAlt: Permission-aware document retrieval feeding a cited business answer.

diagram.caption: A RAG pipeline retrieves permitted source passages before constructing a grounded answer.

articles.title: Agentic Retrieval: Search, Verify and Cite
articles.summary: Add bounded search refinement and evidence verification when a single retrieval pass cannot resolve a multi-part business question.
articles.seoTitle: Agentic Retrieval: Search, Verify and Cite
articles.seoDescription: Design bounded agentic retrieval with query refinement, source verification and claim-level citations. Learn when another search is worthwhile.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

articles.coverConcept: An evidence-gap loop links question decomposition, search, passage verification and claim citation before a stopping gate.
articles.coverAlt: Bounded search and verification loop producing source-supported claims.

diagram.caption: Further retrieval addresses a recorded evidence gap before final synthesis.

modules.title: Tools & Integrations
modules.description: Expose useful operations through validated contracts, scoped APIs and MCP connections.

articles.title: Designing Reliable Tools for AI Agents
articles.summary: Design agent tools around clear operations, validated arguments, useful observations and server-enforced authorization.
articles.seoTitle: Designing Reliable Tools for AI Agents
articles.seoDescription: Design tools with clear names, bounded inputs, scoped access and useful results. Includes a support lookup contract and failure-case exercise.
articles.coverConcept: A tool contract flows through argument validation, authorization, business checks and a typed result with evidence.
articles.coverAlt: Tool execution pipeline with validation, authorization and typed results.

diagram.caption: Useful tool execution requires validation, permission and business-state checks.

articles.title: Connecting Agents to APIs and Databases
articles.summary: Connect agent tools to existing services without exposing arbitrary queries, credentials or another user’s records.
articles.seoTitle: Connecting AI Agents to APIs and Databases
articles.seoDescription: Connect agent tools to APIs and databases with parameterized queries, identity scoping, timeouts and clear failure outcomes.
articles.coverConcept: An authorized agent tool routes to a scoped API adapter or parameterized database query and returns a minimal normalized observation.
articles.coverAlt: Scoped API and database adapters returning normalized tool observations.

diagram.caption: Scoped adapters normalize API and database results without exposing arbitrary queries.

articles.title: Building Your First MCP Integration
articles.summary: Connect a read-only business capability through MCP while keeping host policy, server authorization and tool contracts explicit.
articles.seoTitle: Build Your First MCP Integration for an AI Agent
articles.seoDescription: Learn MCP host, client and server responsibilities. Connect a read-only tool, inspect its contract and test access and failure boundaries.
articles.coverConcept: A host contains an agent and MCP client connected to a read-only MCP server, which checks authorization before accessing order records.
articles.coverAlt: MCP host and client connecting to an authorized read-only order server.

diagram.caption: MCP connects the host to a capability whose server still enforces record authorization.

modules.title: Agent Workflow Patterns
modules.description: Compose predictable stages, bounded planning and deliberate human review.

articles.title: Prompt Chaining, Routing and Parallel Execution
articles.summary: Choose simple composition patterns for multi-step tasks, and define explicit contracts between model-assisted workflow stages.
articles.seoTitle: Prompt Chaining, Routing and Parallel Execution
articles.seoDescription: Compare chaining, routing and parallel execution for AI workflows. Design stage contracts, failure handling and a document-processing example.
articles.coverConcept: An incoming request passes a router to a sequential extraction-validation chain or two independent parallel checks joined at a result gate.
articles.coverAlt: Routing, sequential chaining and parallel checks in one workflow.

diagram.caption: A fixed workflow joins independent checks after structured extraction.

articles.title: Planning, Tool Use and Feedback Loops
articles.summary: Design short, revisable plans that connect agent actions to observations, verification and explicit stopping conditions.
articles.seoTitle: Planning, Tool Use and Feedback Loops for Agents
articles.seoDescription: Build bounded agent planning loops with evidence-based next steps, verification and stopping rules. Includes a delivery investigation exercise.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

articles.coverConcept: A task goal produces a short plan, selected tool action and observation, followed by verification that either revises the plan or ends the run.
articles.coverAlt: Planning loop with tool observations, verification and an explicit exit.

diagram.caption: Verification uses observations to revise a plan or justify stopping.

articles.title: Designing Human Review and Escalation
articles.summary: Build useful human handoffs with explicit triggers, evidence bundles and approvals tied to exact proposed actions.
articles.seoTitle: Designing Human Review and Agent Escalation
articles.seoDescription: Design agent handoffs with clear triggers, reviewer evidence, action-specific approvals and reliable resume behavior. Includes a support scenario.
articles.coverConcept: An agent decision reaches a review gate, presents evidence and an exact proposed action, then branches to approve, revise or decline before controlled execution.
articles.coverAlt: Human review gate with evidence, scoped approval and controlled continuation.

diagram.caption: Human approval applies to a specific operation and is rechecked against current state.

modules.title: Multi-Agent Systems
modules.description: Choose justified agent boundaries and coordinate specialist work with explicit contracts and state ownership.

articles.summary: Decide whether specialist agents add useful independence or merely increase coordination, latency and failure modes.
articles.seoTitle: When Should You Use Multiple AI Agents?

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system

articles.coverConcept: A single bounded agent is compared with three independent specialists and a coordinator, each reporting evidence and coordination cost.
articles.coverAlt: Single-agent baseline compared with coordinated specialist agents.

diagram.caption: Compare specialist coordination with a strong single-agent baseline on the same task.

articles.title: Supervisor, Specialist and Handoff Patterns

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system

articles.coverAlt: Supervisor dispatch, validated specialist returns and an explicit handoff.

diagram.caption: A supervisor delegates bounded work and validates specialist results before synthesis.

articles.title: Designing Communication and Shared State
articles.summary: Coordinate specialist agents with versioned messages, explicit state ownership and evidence-preserving conflict handling.
articles.seoTitle: Multi-Agent Communication and Shared State
articles.seoDescription: Design agent messages, shared state and conflict handling. Learn ownership, version checks, evidence provenance and safe aggregation patterns.

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system

articles.coverAlt: Versioned specialist evidence flowing into a consistent shared-state snapshot.

modules.title: Engineering Capstone
modules.description: Specify, implement and package an evidence-based business agent for evaluation and operational review.

articles.title: Define Your Agent’s Requirements and Architecture
articles.summary: Turn a business request into testable agent requirements, evidence contracts, tool boundaries and an implementation-ready architecture.
articles.seoTitle: Define AI Agent Requirements and Architecture
articles.seoDescription: Write testable requirements for an AI agent. Define users, evidence, tools, authorization, outcomes and architecture before implementation.
articles.coverConcept: A business goal is decomposed into user tasks, evidence requirements and permission boundaries, converging into a testable architecture contract.
articles.coverAlt: Business requirements flowing into a testable agent architecture.

diagram.caption: Requirements connect business tasks to evidence, permissions and testable outcomes.

articles.title: Implement an End-to-End Business Workflow
articles.summary: Implement the capstone as small testable adapters, a bounded controller and evidence-aware outputs with a reliable review path.
articles.seoTitle: Implement an End-to-End AI Agent Workflow
articles.seoDescription: Implement a business agent with scoped adapters, structured state, bounded execution, grounded answers and a useful human review path.

articles.coverAlt: End-to-end agent workflow from authentication to answer or review.
